notes: Increased sensor size and spread for better coverage; raised base speed to 1.2 with adjusted PID gains for improved control at higher speed. This aims to reduce line loss on complex tracks and improve overall score.
rationale: The previous iteration's race data shows excellent performance on the oval track with perfect completion, no line loss, and very low RMS error, indicating the controller and geometry work well on simple curves. However, on the s-bend track, the robot went off track with one line loss event and higher RMS error, suggesting the current sensor coverage and control gains are insufficient for sharper curves and higher speeds. To improve robustness, I increased the sensor size from 0.012 to 0.016 to enhance line detection and spread the sensors wider from ±0.04 m to ±0.05 m to cover a broader area, especially useful in sharp turns. I also increased the base speed from 1.0 to 1.2 to test higher speed capability, expecting the controller gains to be adjusted to maintain stability at this speed. The wheel track, wheel radius, body dimensions, and mass remain unchanged to preserve stability and inertia balance. The controller uses a smooth gradient of sensor weights from left to right sensors, with proportional, integral, and derivative gains tuned to balance responsiveness and stability. The line loss strategy is set to 'search_left' to steer right when the line is lost, which worked well previously. I request measurements of completion, progress, line_loss_events, rms_error, and completion_time to evaluate performance comprehensively.
